articles.title: The Big Beautiful Boycott: Starbucks Workers’ Fight for a First Contract
articles.author: Ian M.
articles.content_excerpt: After five years of strikes, marches on the boss, petitions, and legal action, Starbucks Workers United (SBWU) called for a boycott in August. Beyond individual coffee drinkers, the union is asking universities, other unions, candidates, and political organizations to sign on to the boycott campaign. Boycotts have a long history in the labor movement but can be risky. They rely on external support, and if they fail to make a dent in the company’s bottom line, they risk undercutting the momentum of the movement. Luckily for SBWU, unions are more popular than ever, and we’ve already seen that plenty of people are ready to throw down to support their baristas. articles.title: An Effective AI Pushback Has to Go Beyond the Local
articles.author: Aziz Huq
articles.content_excerpt: Last week’s election returns embodied a broad, national, and bipartisan reaction against data centers. In forty-six of the forty-seven local referenda held across some thirteen states, voters rejected new data center construction. Public opposition reflects local concerns about water usage, grid sustainability, and noise pollution. This opposition is also bubbling up at a moment when most of the public distrust s artificial intelligence (AI) in general, when two-thirds of Americans hold negative views of AI firms and their close ties to the Trump administration, and when fears about AI rank high among Americans’ leading worries. articles.title: The Parish of Seeds
articles.author: Jason Collins
articles.content_excerpt: Moira’s Parish of Seeds had been born from the bones of a megachurch that was once known for its large and loud worship sessions. Inside, Moira and her crew had torn out the pews and converted the sanctuary into a seed-curing room. The baptismal font became a hydroponic lettuce tank, and the stained-glass Jesus now watched over shelves of okra, collards, and marigold seeds. Read more via Scalawag : The Parish of Seeds .

articles.author: Joe Simpson
articles.content_excerpt: RECAP: 2026 Member Mobilization Institute ONAWAY, MI – UAW members from across the country gathered at Black Lake for the 2026 Member Mobilization Institute, a week of learning new skills, sharing ideas, and exploring how we can strengthen our union together. Workshops, discussions, and hands-on practice challenged participants to consider what it takes to build lasting power and to prepare for the opportunities and challenges ahead, including May Day 2028. Learning continued beyond the classroom as delegates embraced opportunities to share their own worker stories by creating art with block printing, bandanas, signs, buttons, photography, and zines. articles.title: California UFCW Leaders Really Don’t Want Union Elections
articles.author: Lisa Xu
articles.content_excerpt: In a union that has been headed by one family with no competitive elections since 1984, a group of grocery workers is organizing for change. But last week, they say, union staff who back the incumbent administration went to outrageous lengths in an attempt to make sure there’s no election this year either. On the afternoon of Monday, November 2, Eric Marcuz, a veteran Northern California Safeway worker, stopped at the union office to pick up blank petitions to get on the ballot in the union’s upcoming election. Marcuz is running for president on the At What Cost slate in the 23,000-member United Food and Commercial Workers (UFCW) Local 8–Golden State (8-GS), one of the largest locals in the union. articles.title: Vicious Racial Undertow
articles.author: Mark P. Fancher
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. When the big blue wave came crashing through the most unlikely regions of the country, it washed ashore a remarkable group of newly elected racial, ethnic, gender and religious “firsts.” Progressives were of course gleeful. But if America’s history is any guide, joy about racial electoral breakthroughs may be premature. There is a well-established record of this country riding waves of legal and political progress toward the racial ideal, but at the same time being pulled backwards by a social undertow driven by white racists. articles.title: Reactionary Feminists Offer Bad Solutions to Real Problems
articles.author: Kaja Kröger
articles.content_excerpt: To more and more people, the promises of sex-positive liberal feminism feel empty. The sexual ideas that have dominated feminism in the last two decades — including that sexual liberation always serves women’s interests, that consent is the only relevant sexual ethic, and that consuming porn and buying sex are benign practices like any other — are beginning to ring hollow. In this context, an emergent theoretical strand with the pointed, self-chosen name “reactionary feminism” has drawn considerable attention. It calls into question the liberal assertion that every form of sexual morality is anti-feminist — a view the Left has absorbed in recent decades. articles.title: The Dollar’s Power Never Came From Oil
articles.author: Matías Vernengo
articles.content_excerpt: The war in Iran and the disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz have renewed an old debate about the foundations of American global power. Oil has been central to the geopolitical order dominated by the United States since World War II. The dollar is the principal international currency, oil is overwhelmingly priced in dollars, and American military power has been essential to controlling access to petroleum, particularly in the Middle East. The question raised by some analysts is whether the erosion of this arrangement, accelerated by the transition to cleaner sources of energy, signals the end of American hegemony and of the privileged position of the dollar.
